published_statement: CODATA 2018 and 2022 recommended values (NIST tables): c = 299 792 458 m s^-1 (exact); G = 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 (u_r = 2.2e-5; identical in 2018 and 2022); g_n = 9.806 65 m s^-2 (exact, conventional standard acceleration of gravity). IAU 2012 B2: au = 149 597 870 700 m exactly. IAU 2015 B3: nominal solar mass parameter GM_sun = 1.3271244 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2 (exact conversion constant); the solar mass in kg is not a nominal constant but GM_sun/G, carrying G's uncertainty (astropy encodes exactly this).
published_hypotheses: c and g_n are exact by definition (c fixes the metre since 1983; g_n is a conventional value, not a local measured gravity).
au is exact by definition (IAU 2012 B2), not a measured Earth-Sun distance.

G is a least-squares-adjusted measured value with standard uncertainty 0.00015e-11 (u_r 2.2e-5); the input G data are mutually inconsistent and CODATA applies an expansion factor to them (the factor itself is NAMED-NOT-READ here; a web-search snippet of the CODATA 2022 text gives 3.9 over 16 input data, not read at source).
M_sun in kg is DERIVED as nominal GM_sun / G, so its kg value is tied to whichever G is used and carries G's u_r; only GM_sun is known to ~1e-10.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What was lacking: G is the least-well-known constant CODATA recommends (u_r 2.2e-5) and its input measurements are mutually inconsistent beyond their stated uncertainties (the published G history read here: 6.67428 (2006), 6.67384 (2010), 6.67408 (2014), 6.67430 (2018, 2022) -- a 6.9e-5 spread of recommended values, and the 2010 value sits 3.1 sigma(2018) below the 2018 one). So 'previous physicists lacked data' is literally true of G and is why its recommended value moved at each of the three adjustments 2006-2010, 2010-2014, 2014-2018 (unchanged 2018-2022). Does having more data change wall.py's conclusion? Evidence, computed: no. The figures wall.py draws conclusions from depend on G at most as G^1, and several (the 14-orders inversion, the AU radii, the areal density, and the Msun figures when M_sun is taken consistently as GM_sun/G) do not depend on G at all; a +-1000 ppm move -- about 14x the whole 2006-2022 spread and ~45x u_r -- leaves every conclusion and every order of magnitude in place. The other four inputs lack nothing: c, g_n and the au are definitions, and GM_sun is known to ~1e-10. The one datum wall.py is behind on is its own M_sun: 1.98847e30 is the pre-2019 (G-2014-derived) value, and pairing it with the 2018 G misplaces the Msun figures by 3.0e-5 -- recorded as a discrepancy, it changes no printed digit. Context outside this entry's owner, recorded not graded: shipspec.py:26, kerr.py:40 and navigate.py:36 use M_sun = 1.98892e30, which equals GM_sun/G only for G = 6.6726e-11 (the CODATA-1986-era G), i.e. a 2.6e-4 inconsistency with their own G = 6.67430e-11.
grade_evidence: c, g_n and au are exact by definition and wall.py uses them exactly and in the defined sense (wall.py:242, 566, 650). G = 6.67430e-11 at wall.py:441 is the CODATA 2018 value and is unchanged in CODATA 2022 (NIST tables, READ via scipy 1.17.1 transcription). The re-derivation (exit 0) shows every wall.py dimensional conclusion is invariant under every recommended G since 2006, under +-1 sigma, and under a +-1000 ppm stress; the G-exponents are computed symbolically from wall.py's own formulas. The only moved datum is M_sun: wall.py's 1.98847e30 is GM_sun/G(2014), inconsistent with its own G by +3.0e-5 -- a DISCREPANCY that shifts the Msun figures below their printed precision and inside the selftest tolerances; it is not a refutation and does not narrow the use. Limitation on the grade, named: the CODATA and IAU documents were read only through verbatim machine transcriptions of their tables (scipy, astropy), not the papers' prose, because alphaXiv was over quota and arxiv/NIST are egress-blocked; the grade rests on the values, which is what this entry uses.
what_would_change_the_grade: (a) A future CODATA G moving by more than ~0.5% (500x its present u_r; no recommended value since 2006 has moved more than 7e-5) could move the 965 m / 4.48 km rounding but still not the conclusions -- it would take an order-of-magnitude change in G to move any conclusion, so no plausible datum changes STANDS to DATA-DEPENDENT. (b) Reading the CODATA 2022 paper at source and finding the tree's G used outside its stated scope would change the read status, not, on present evidence, the grade. (c) If a downstream owner relies on the Msun figures to better than 3e-5, the M_sun/G pairing discrepancy would become material and should be graded NARROWED for that owner.
